Shri Ankur Mody, learned Additional Advocate General for r  ORDER Per: Justice Pushpendra Yadav

By way of this intra-court appeal filed under Section 2 (1) of the Madhya Pradesh Uchcha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyaypeeth Ko Appeal) Adhiniyam, 2005, appellant is challenging the order dated 05.12.2024 passed in W.P.No.25093/2024 whereby the writ petition filed by the appellant herein was dismissed.

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts of the case are that the appellant herein is working as Head Constable in the respondents' department.

On 04.05.2024, an FIR was registered against him bearing Crime No.170/2024 in Police Station Mahila Thana Padav, District Gwalior for the offence under Sections 376 (2)(n) and 506 of IPC for committing rape against the complainant multiple times between September 2022 to April 2024.

Consequent upon registration of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:32494 2 WA-515-2025 FIR, appellant was placed under suspension vide order dated 05.05.2024.
Subsequently, a notice dated 09.08.2024 was issued by which he was called upon to give his statement in preliminary inquiry.

The order of suspension and letter dated 09.08.2024 was challenged by the appellant in writ petition mainly on the ground that on account of registration of criminal case, appellant has been placed under suspension but the same was continued without application of mind.

The respondents have also initiated the departmental inquiry which amounts to Gabbar Singh vs Director General Of Police on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118954941/
1 double jeopardy.
3.

sentences.text:
It was the case of appellant before the learned writ Court that the investigation in a criminal case has been completed and framing of charge will take time and trial would take further time therefore,
appellant cannot be placed under suspension for such a long time.
Learned writ Court by impugned order, dismissed the writ petition, hence the present appeal.
In the present appeal, appellant has also prayed for stay of the charge-sheet issued during the pendency of writ petition.

In the present appeal, learned counsel for the appellant confined his argument mainly on the ground that the departmental proceeding and criminal case are based on the same set of facts, therefore,
departmental proceeding should not be initiated against the appellant.
If appellant discloses the evidence in departmental proceedings same will cause serious prejudice to the appellant in criminal case.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was placed under suspension on account of registration of a criminal case and now appellant has been unnecessarily targeted by initiation of departmental inquiry which is unconstitutional.

The appellant has relied upon the order NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:32494 3 WA-515-2025 passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Capt. M. Paul Anthony Vs. Bharat Gold Mines Ltd. & Anr. reported in AIR 1999 SC 1416 .

entities.text: Capt. M. Paul Anthony Vs. Bharat Gold Mines Ltd. & Anr. reported in AIR 1999 SC 1416
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/State supported the order passed by learned writ Court and argued that there is no bar to conduct disciplinary proceedings and criminal trial simultaneously and prayed for dismissal of appeal.

6. Heard the counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

In the present appeal, the appellant has prayed for stay of departmental proceeding on the ground that on the same set of facts, criminal case is also pending but appellant neither challenged the charge-sheet of departmental enquiry before the writ Court nor before this Court.
In the writ petition, the appellant challenged the letter dated 09.08.2024 by which he was called upon to give his statement in his preliminary inquiry.

After completing the preliminary inquiry, charge-sheet was issued to the appellant on 15.01.2025 but the said charge-sheet was not challenged by the appellant neither in the writ Court nor before this Court.
In absence of challenge to the charge-sheet, question of grant of stay does not arise.

8. As per charge-sheet the charges levelled against the appellant are as under:-
(i) While in departmental service, by committing a criminal act with a woman,
displaying
serious misconduct of the category of moral turpitude, tarnishing the image of the police department and displaying conduct unworthy of the police service

. 
(ii) Displaying indiscipline and arbitrariness by clearly disobeying the lawful order of the senior officer by not NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:32494 4 Gabbar Singh vs Director General Of Police on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118954941/
2 WA-515-2025

entities.text: Gabbar Singh vs Director General Of Police on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: submitting the reply till the date of issue of charge-sheet even after giving sufficient opportunity to submit the reply by issuing a show cause notice.

(iii) Conduct contrary to the police service rules and violating the provisions mentioned in Police Rules Para 64 (03), (04), (11).
9.

So far as the ground raised by the appellant that during the pendency of criminal trial,
departmental inquiry should not be continued is concerned, it is the considered opinion of this Court, there is no legal bar to conduct disciplinary proceeding and criminal trail simultaneously.
10. So far as the criminal case is concerned, the same is pending against the appellant for the offence under Sections 376 (2) (n), 506 and 377 of IPC.
From perusal of the charges levelled against the appellant in departmental enquiry, it is clear that the same is not absolutely identical.
The purpose underlying departmental proceedings is distinctly different from the purpose behind prosecution of offenders for commission of offences by them.

11. The reliance placed by counsel for the appellant in the case of Capt. M. Paul Anthony (supra) in which Hon'ble Supreme Court in Para-22 held as under:-
"(i) Departmental proceedings and proceedings in a criminal case can proceed simultaneously as there is no bar in their being conducted simultaneously, though separately.

(ii) If the departmental proceedings and the criminal case are based on identical and similar set of facts and the charge in the criminal case against the delinquent employee is of a grave nature which involves complicated questions of law and fact, it would be desirable to stay the departmental proceedings till the conclusion NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:32494 5 WA-515-2025 of the criminal case.

(iii) Whether the nature of a charge in a criminal case is grave and whether complicated questions of fact and law are involved in that case, will depend upon the nature of offence, the nature of the case launched against the employee on the basis of evidence and material collected against him during investigation or as reflected in the charge sheet.

(iv) The factors mentioned at (ii) and (iii) above cannot be considered in isolation to stay the Departmental proceedings but due regard has to be given to the fact that the departmental proceedings cannot be unduly delayed.

(v) If the criminal case does not proceed or its disposal is being unduly delayed, the departmental proceedings, even if they were stayed on account of the pendency of the criminal case, can be resumed and proceeded with so as to conclude them at an early date, so that if the employee is found not guilty his honor may be vindicated and in Gabbar Singh vs Director General Of Police on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118954941/
3 case he is found guilty, administration may get rid of him at the earliest."
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the case of Capt. M. Paul Anthony (supra) , the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that if the departmental proceedings and the criminal case are based on identical and similar set of facts and the charges in the criminal case against the delinquent employee is of a grave nature which involves complicated question of law and fact, it would be desirable to stay the departmental proceedings till the conclusion of the criminal case.
13.
In the present case, the charges of departmental proceedings are not absolutely identical to the charges in the criminal case.
Moreover, from the pleadings, the appellant has completely failed to establish that criminal case against him is of a grave nature which involves complected questions of law and fact.
In absence of establishing such facts, the departmental proceedings cannot be stayed in a routine and casual manner.

The appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:32494 6 WA-515-2025 has failed to establish his case within the four corners of the directions issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Capt. M. Paul Anthony (supra) .

14. In the case of Depot Manager, Andhra Pradesh State vs Mohd. Yousuf Miya Etc. reported in 1997 (2) SCC 699, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the purpose underlying departmental proceedings is distinctly different from the purpose behind prosecution of offenders for commission of offence by them.

entities.text: Depot Manager, Andhra Pradesh State vs Mohd. Yousuf Miya Etc. reported in 1997 (2) SCC 699
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While criminal prosecution for an offence is launched for violation of a duty that the offender owes to the society, departmental enquiry is aimed at maintaining discipline and efficiency in service.

The difference in the standard of proof and the application of the rules of evidence to one and in applicability to the other was also explained and highlighted only to explain that conceptually the two operate in different spheres and are intended to serve distinctly different purposes.

15. After considering the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Capt. M. Paul Anthony (supra) , in the case of Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. & vs Sarvesh Berry reported in 2005(10) SCC 471 has held as under:-
"8. A crime is an act of commission in violation of law or of omission of public duty.

entities.text: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. & vs Sarvesh Berry reported in 2005(10) SCC 471
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The departmental enquiry is to maintain discipline in the service and efficiency of public service.
It would, therefore, be expedient that the disciplinary proceedings are conducted and completed as expeditiously as possible.

It is not, therefore, desirable to lay down any guidelines as inflexible rules in which the departmental proceedings may or may not be stayed pending trial in criminal case against the delinquent officer.
Each case NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:32494 7 WA-515-2025 requires to be considered in the backdrop of its own facts and circumstances.

There would be no bar to proceed simultaneously with departmental enquiry and trial of a criminal case unless the charge in the criminal trial is of a grave nature involving complicated questions of fact and law.....
Under these circumstances, what is required to be seen is whether the departmental enquiry would seriously prejudice the delinquent in his defense at the trial in a criminal case.

It is always a question of fact to be considered in each case depending on its own facts Gabbar Singh vs Director General Of Police on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118954941/
4 and circumstances."
16.

entities.text: Gabbar Singh vs Director General Of Police on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of M/s Stanzen Toyotetsu India P. Ltd. Versus Girish V &
Ors. reported in 2014 (3) SCC 636 has held as under:-
" It is unnecessary to multiply decisions on the subject for the legal position as emerging from the above pronouncements and the earlier pronouncements of this Court in a large number of similar cases is well settled that disciplinary proceedings and proceedings in a criminal case can proceed simultaneously in the absence of any legal bar to such simultaneity.

entities.text:
M/s Stanzen Toyotetsu India P. Ltd. Versus Girish V &
Ors. reported in 2014 (3) SCC 636
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also evident that while seriousness of the charge leveled against the employees is a consideration, the same is not by itself sufficient unless the case also involves complicated questions of law and fact.

Even when the charge is found to be serious and complicated questions of fact and law that arise for consideration, the Court will have to keep in mind the fact that departmental proceedings cannot be suspended indefinitely or delayed unduly."

17. From the legal settled position of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is clear that there is no legal bar to conduct disciplinary NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:32494 8 WA-515-2025 proceeding and criminal trial simultaneously.

Therefore also, no case is made out warranting interference as the appellant has not challenged the charge- sheet neither before the writ Court nor before this Court nor has established by way of pleadings or otherwise that complicated question of law and fact was involved in the criminal case and disclosure of evidence in departmental inquiry will seriously prejudice his defense in a criminal case.
The charges levelled against the appellant in a departmental inquiry are also not absolutely identical therefore, no case is made out warranting interference.
Learned writ Court has rightly dismissed the petition.

Hence,
order passed by writ Court is hereby affirmed.
Writ appeal is dismissed.

(ANAND PATHAK) (PUSHPENDRA  JUDGE JUDG  Ashish*
